entry.title: OpenAI publishes new mathematical results from internal frontier model with Lean proof formalizations and research details on GitHub [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has released a collection of new mathematical findings generated by an internal frontier AI model, sharing the results publicly on GitHub. The release includes formalized proofs in the Lean programming language and detailed documentation of the model's reasoning and computational resources used. The company collaborated with the Institute for Advanced Study's Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence to develop best practices for sharing these results. OpenAI plans to fund workshops and programs to further explore and understand AI-produced mathematical advancements and aims to responsibly release the model behind these findings while continuing to refine disclosure standards based on community feedback.

entry.title: Google DeepMind launches EmbeddingGemma 2, a 740M-parameter open-source multimodal embedding model for on-device text, image, audio, and video processing [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google DeepMind has released EmbeddingGemma 2, an open-source multimodal embedding model designed for efficient on-device inference across text, images, audio, and video. With 740 million parameters and built on the Gemma 4 architecture, the model supports unified embedding spaces for various data types and is optimized for resource-constrained hardware, enabling privacy-preserving and low-latency applications. EmbeddingGemma 2 improves code embedding performance significantly and matches or outperforms larger models on multiple benchmarks while offering modularity and storage efficiency through dynamic vector truncation. It supports an extended 8K token context window and integrates with generative models like Gemma 4 to facilitate on-device retrieval augmented generation (RAG) pipelines. The model is available under an Apache 2.0 license with weights accessible on Hugging Face and Kaggle.

entry.title: Simon Willison tests Mistral Large 4 and other LLMs generating SVGs of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Simon Willison shared a comment on Hacker News about the saturation of benchmarks for frontier language models, illustrating this by prompting several models, including Mistral Large 4, to generate an SVG image of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars. This playful test highlights the current state of AI model evaluation and reasoning capabilities. The models tested alongside Mistral Large 4 included Claude Opus 5.5, GPT 6.1 Sol, and Gemini 3.8 Flash, with their default reasoning levels compared through a visualization tool. The discussion reflects ongoing conversations about the challenges in benchmarking advanced AI systems as they reach similar performance levels on standard tests.

entry.title: OpenTPU launches open-source AI accelerator designed by AI, running multiple modern models on FPGA with bit-exact simulation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenTPU is an open-source AI accelerator project developed using AI to design hardware that runs its own inference. It includes a complete hardware design, instruction set, simulator, compiler, and host software, enabling users to understand AI accelerator internals from hardware to software. The accelerator runs ten modern AI models on an FPGA card, producing bit-for-bit identical outputs to its simulator, demonstrating practical performance and accuracy. The design operates on a Xilinx Kintex-7 FPGA with DDR3 memory, supporting models up to 35 billion parameters using mixture-of-experts techniques with expert data streamed from host storage. It uses 4-bit and int8 quantization to optimize memory and speed, achieving up to 45% faster decoding speeds with minimal accuracy loss. The project serves both as a functional AI accelerator and a learning resource for hardware and software integration in AI systems.

entry.title: OpenAI launches Decisions API public beta with gpt-6-luna model for faster text and image evaluation [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has introduced the Decisions API in public beta, offering about 10 times faster evaluation of text, images, or both compared to its Responses API. The API returns typed answers such as probabilities, choices from fixed sets, or scores against rubrics, enabling applications to classify content, route requests, and prioritize work more efficiently. The Decisions API uses the gpt-6-luna model and supports predicate, choice, and score question types to assess conditions, select categories, or rate ordered levels. It accepts combined text and base64-encoded images as input and provides probability estimates to guide automated decisions. OpenAI expects to move the API to general availability in the coming weeks.

entry.title: Utah allows AI to examine patients and prescribe acne medication without direct doctor oversight in a limited one-year pilot [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Utah has launched a one-year pilot program permitting a healthcare startup, Nolla Health, to use AI to examine patients with mild-to-moderate acne and prescribe medication without direct human oversight. The program starts with AI analyzing patient-submitted facial scans and medical histories to recommend treatments from a list of eight approved topical medications. The pilot includes phased oversight: the first 100 prescriptions require doctor review before pharmacy submission, the next 400 prescriptions are submitted by AI with weekly retrospective physician review, and thereafter doctors review at least 10% of prescriptions monthly. The program aims to explore AI's role in treating less serious conditions while limiting risks associated with AI medical advice.

entry.title: Report: Over 2,000 legal cases involve AI hallucinations in court filings, with courts emphasizing verification and accountability over disclosure [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Legal cases involving AI hallucinations in court filings have surpassed 2,000, predominantly in the United States. Courts are increasingly focusing on verification of AI-generated content rather than mere disclosure, with penalties ranging from fines to license suspensions, especially for lawyers. New judicial rules, such as Iowa's 2027 prohibition on judges delegating decision-making to AI, reflect growing regulatory responses. The majority of AI-related filings come from pro se litigants and lawyers, with courts imposing stricter sanctions on legal professionals. While some advocate for banning AI in legal work, the consensus leans toward maintaining accountability for AI use rather than outright prohibition, recognizing AI's potential to improve access to justice if properly managed.

entry.title: Epoch.ai reports AI performance costs have fallen 47% per quarter since 2023, outpacing other transformative technologies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Epoch.ai analyzed AI performance benchmarks from the past three years and found that the cost to achieve a given level of AI capability has dropped about 47% per quarter, or 13 times per year, since 2023. This rate of decline is significantly faster than historical price drops in technologies like DNA sequencing, computing, lithium batteries, and electricity. The study highlights that price reductions vary by domain, with math problems seeing faster cost declines than game-based puzzles, and that prices fall most rapidly immediately after a new performance level is first achieved. The analysis is based on five AI benchmarks covering mathematics, hard sciences, and games of skill, and includes data such as OpenAI's GPT models reducing the cost per question on a PhD-level science exam by over 700 times in under 18 months. The report notes caveats including potential benchmark-specific training and differences between benchmark performance and real-world utility. Despite these limitations, the findings suggest that the "price of thought" in AI is decreasing at an unprecedented pace compared to other general-purpose technologies.

entry.title: Musubi launches PolicyLM-1.7B, a lightweight AI decision model for real-time content moderation with open weights [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Musubi announced PolicyLM-1.7B, a lightweight AI decision model designed for real-time content moderation that applies plain English policies to messages in under 50 milliseconds. The model offers flexibility similar to large language models but runs at speeds and costs comparable to existing AI classifiers, allowing platform managers to label content proactively without retraining when policies change. The model outputs binary judgments to determine if content fits a category, enabling scalable and customizable moderation. Musubi's approach builds on earlier decision model concepts and aims to provide an open, self-hosted alternative to recent decision models from companies like OpenAI and Amazon, highlighting the potential for AI to improve content moderation on social platforms.

entry.summary: My comment on EmbeddingGemma 2 - Hacker News. I really appreciate that EmbeddingGemma 2 is under the Apache 2.0 license. For embedding models in particular, I don't think it makes sense to use a closed, proprietary, hosted-only model. Most applications of embedding models involve calculating thousands or even millions of embedding vectors and storing them for later comparison. If your model is proprietary, the vendor is likely someday going to decide to stop offering that model. They'll have a better model to replace it, but you still need to pay to re-calculate those millions of stored existing vectors. (In April 2024 OpenAI offered to "cover the financial cost of users re-embedding content with these new models" - https://openai.com/index/gpt-4-api-general-availability/ - but I don't think that's something we can rely on from every provider.) Notably, I don't want to host the model myself. I'd much rather pay a provider for a hosted model while knowing that if they ever stop hosting it I can run the open weights version myself - or find another vendor who can do that for me. Tags: google, ai, generative-ai, embeddings, gemma

entry.title: Introducing Mistral Large 4: Le chonk [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Introducing Mistral Large 4: Le chonk Mistral are back in the game. Today they're releasing a preview of Mistral Large 4, a 1 trillion parameter, 49 billion active parameter model trained on their own cluster of 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The preview is available via their API. They promise to release the open weights model at the "end of this month". The model only supports two reasoning levels - "none" and "high" - via the Mistral API. Here are both pelicans - the "high" one looks better, though surprisingly it only used 2,717 output tokens compared to "none" which used 3,275: On Artificial Analysis it scores 38, just behind DeepSeek 4.1 Flash, which is a 552B model. It's a huge improvement on last December's Mistral Large 3, which drew this terrible pelican and scored 9 on AA. It's certainly not a Fable-class model, but it's great to see Mistral put out a model that's back to being maybe about 6 months behind the frontier. Via Hacker News Tags: ai, generative-ai, llms, mistral, pelican-riding-a-bicycle, llm-release

entry.title: AI Whistleblowers Say Researchers Are Checking AI Less Frequently [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: It won't be any surprise to people with human intelligence that Monday's New York City Council hearing on the risks of AI was as theatrical as a Broadway show. What was more surprising was what the AI researchers testified about how AI research is evolving, and what that means for their job. For those who missed it, the city council heard testimony from three AI lab whistleblowers: Jacob Coxon, formerly of Anthropic and OpenAI; Alex Turner, formerly of Google DeepMind; and Daniel Kokotajlo, formerly of OpenAI. Afterwards, they heard from representatives of the AI labs. We'll get to that lower down. One of the most interesting parts of the whistleblowers' testimony related to the AI research process. Coxon and Kokotajlo each said that researchers at the labs have lately been letting AI drive the process of writing code and research. Researchers check AI's work less frequently, they said. The labs might not agree with that exact characterization, although their representatives weren't asked about it at the hearing. But the labs have been the first to say that AI has greatly accelerated the process of AI research. Anthropic even said in a report last month that, as of August, AI was leading more than a quarter of model research and development at the company.

entry.title: Why the SaaSpocalypse Isn't Over For Workday [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: AI doesn't seem likely to completely replace enterprise apps like Workday, which companies use to store key information about employees and financial transactions. But it is putting potential constraints on their growth. Already, some Workday customers are using so-called AI agents from Anthropic, Microsoft and other providers to pull data from Workday so they can analyze employment records or trends, for example, meaning the customers themselves don't have to visit the app. And many companies that pay for access to Workday's own AI tools, which sit on top of its core HR and finance databases, aren't regularly using them, according to interviews with five consultants and partners that work with more than 2,000 Workday customers.
